recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit as-is. No core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-31520 unless BRR later changes the OR semantics or asks for different wording.
issue_request: FHIR-31520 was an Applied/Persuasive BRR change request for the R5 ClinicalUseIssue artifact asking that the repeating comorbidity elements under indication and contraindication clarify whether multiple entries are AND or OR. The Jira resolution says to document that repeats are interpreted as OR.
initial_application: The active resource is now ClinicalUseDefinition. Historical source commits 9fe57dc4a4d48a9412d5acd03271d5153327477d and a0d2c7eabe5f0540f74239fee191477d72c28209 added the OR wording to ClinicalUseDefinition.indication.comorbidity and ClinicalUseDefinition.contraindication.comorbidity respectively.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists ClinicalUseDefinition as an active BRR-owned normative resource and leaves ClinicalUseIssue only as a commented historical name. BRR 2021-10-21 minutes confirm the FHIR-31520 Persuasive vote 5-0-2. FHIR-48893 was mixed into the first historical implementation commit but is already audited separately on the combined branch; FHIR-30176 is only background for the comorbidity datatype.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The combined branch already contains the historical application commits, and the current StructureDefinition definitions at source/clinicalusedefinition/structuredefinition-ClinicalUseDefinition.xml:463 and :703 state that when comorbidity repeats, any one entry is relevant rather than all needing to be present.

related_jiras.note: The first historical source commit combined FHIR-31520 indication wording with separate ClinicalUseDefinition type/backbone invariant work; FHIR-48893 already has its own combined-branch audit commit.
Earlier Published ClinicalUseIssue work changed comorbidity-related elements to CodeableReference(ObservationDefinition), but it did not decide the OR/AND semantics reconciled here.
